free_tier.stated: 291 MB per track to start ('It starts out at 291MB per track .. Once you've made a few sales through Bandcamp (totaling $20 USD or more), we increase the max per-track upload size to 600 megs'), and crucially 'There is no limit on the size of albums'. So total capacity is unbounded at 291 MB x unlimited tracks.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free streaming and free downloads to fans; Bandcamp takes 15% of sales (10% after $5k) but there is no storage or egress bill, and a $0-priced release generates none of that.

tooling: No public API, no bulk uploader. Web album editor only ('Click + add in the top toolbar'). This is the weakest tooling story in the slot.
chaining: Unlimited albums per artist account x unlimited tracks per album x 291 MB per track. The 291 MB cap is per track, and an album has no cap, so a 20-track album is ~5.8 GB before you need anything else.
limits_note: Audio must be 'at least 16-bit, 44.1 kHz lossless files (WAV, AIFF, or FLAC), in stereo (no mono- or multi-channel audio)'. So no MP3 uploads at all. Pro ($10/mo, not free) raises the per-track cap to 2 GB and adds video (500 MB). Free accounts can't upload video.

reliability_note: Lossless masters are kept and fans who buy get the original format; streams are transcoded mp3. The lossless-only requirement is actually a positive for this use case (nothing is lossy-transcoded on the way in), but the 'no multi-channel / no mono' rule rejects perfectly good files, and a release is public the moment it's published. There is no private/unlisted storage mode.
